Thanks — the sequencing looks reasonable. A few legal notes we need to capture explicitly in the MAP so procurement has visibility:

1) DPA timing and scoping: We will provide Redwood's standard DPA attached with guidance on sections we cannot move (data processor liability, incident notification). If Vanguard returns a redline we will review and aim to respond within 3 business days for minor edits; substantial legal amendments (new data residency clauses, third-party subprocessors list changes) will require ~5 business days.

2) Evidence package: SOC2 Type II report (latest) + a sanitized data flow diagram and subprocessor list. We can share SOC2 by 9/22 if NDAs are in place — recommend Vanguard confirm the recipient list for evidence delivery.

3) Order Form and billing: Order Form must include final billing cadence, committed token/embedding blocks, and an initial run-rate. Any change to billing cadence after countersignature requires a written amendment.

4) Roll-forward fallback: Suggest we build a fallback clause in the MAP — if DPA redline pushes the critical path we will accept a conditional signature on commercially binding points while legal finishes DPA negotiation; an internal legal exec approval will be required.

I attached a short guidance doc that lists typical redline requests we expect and our recommended responses.

Attachments: DPA_redline_guidance.docx (docx)

Laura Bennett
Senior Counsel, Commercial Contracts | Redwood Inference
laura@redwood.com
